match.reason: None of the bank points teaches using financial and non-financial performance indicators, such as profit and customer complaints shown in graphs, to judge how a business is going; the closest, the monitoring part of the strategic role of financial management, is broader and does not cover indicators or graphs.

draft.title: Measuring performance
card: a measure in dollars, such as net profit, revenue or expenses.
a measure not in dollars, such as customer complaints, staff turnover or the number of new clients.
Owners compare indicators over time, often on a graph. A line graph shows a trend, and a column graph compares amounts.
Using both kinds gives a fuller view. Profit may be rising while complaints also rise, which could be a warning sign.
draft.remember: Financial and non-financial indicators together show how a business is going.

a.q: Which of these is a non-financial indicator of performance?
opts: The number of customer complaints
Net profit for the year
Revenue from fees
Total wages expense
a.why: Customer complaints are counted, not measured in dollars, so they are non-financial. Profit, revenue and wages are all dollar amounts, so they are financial.
a.clue: Which one is not an amount of money?

b.q: Nina runs a cleaning service in Ballarat. Over six months her net profit rose each month, but the number of client complaints also rose each month. What does this suggest?
opts: Profit looks good, but service quality may be falling
The business is performing well on every measure
The business is making a loss each month
Complaints do not matter if profit is rising
b.why: Rising profit is a good financial sign, but rising complaints is a poor non-financial sign. Looking at both shows a possible problem that profit alone would hide.
b.clue: One indicator is improving and the other is getting worse.

b.best: Profit looks good, but service quality may be falling

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only hedged one ('may be falling'). The other three are flat or absolute claims, so a student could pick it without understanding the idea.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate and match the point. The one minor issue is that question b's right option stands out as the longest and the only hedged choice.
